claims.statement: ConfigResolver produces legacy RockstreamConfig, NodeConfig, diagnostics and dotted-key origins with precedence defaults < selected file < recognized environment variables < supplied CLI overrides; file discovery is explicit path, ROCKSTREAM_CONFIG, then existing ./rockstream.toml.

The resolver errors on an explicitly missing file but skips a missing environment-selected path, resolves file-relative NodeConfig storage URLs against the file parent, and synchronizes canonical/legacy file origins.

Environment configuration is handled through explicit recognized mappings, including ROCKSTREAM_WORKER_EXECUTION_THREADS as a compatibility override, rather than generic binding of every configuration field.
config validate validates the selected file, rejects missing selected files and invalid reports, and optionally checks referenced files; its strict argument is currently unused.

ConfigResolver collects file-validation and final semantic diagnostics without requiring a valid report before returning Ok; startup discards those diagnostics, so successful resolution is not a validation guarantee and unsuccessful file parsing can leave defaults.

Effective text configuration can include source-origin comments and selectively redacts auth secret and sensitive-looking gateway key paths, while effective JSON directly serializes ResolvedConfig rather than the redacted copies.

The executable start path resolves with no explicit config file and supplies defaulted role, listen and auth arguments as CLI overrides; storage is required, and several live StartOptions fields come directly from arguments instead of being read back from resolved NodeConfig.

Live consumers include worker-role Tokio execution_threads, gateway join strategy and webhook listener, typed-management NodeConfig snapshot, and explicit-or-cluster shutdown timeout; accepted configuration alone does not establish wiring of other settings.

Workload application status distinguishes requested policy from actual gateway-local budget limit and usage; worker_effective_revision remains NULL and assigned views report worker_ack_unavailable rather than implying remote application from catalog revision.

run_start validates role, platform, removed cold-tier settings, auth mode and worker/frontier control requirements, and parses SQL, metrics and management addresses before creating storage and audit resources.

The all role starts an ephemeral loopback embedded control service and a worker, requests shard 0 through the normal lease flow and attempts to share its database with the gateway; if no shared shard was obtained gateway startup falls back to opening its own shard.

The control role composes topology/shard management, frontier aggregation and persistent shard/topology/migration stores; Raft gating is attached only when peers are supplied, requiring node ID and Raft bind.
Control stores use a filesystem-backed object store at the shared-storage option or private fallback, but Raft term/vote persistence always stays under the node's private storage/raft directory.

Worker startup requires control, retries connection a bounded number of times, and starts asynchronous registration carrying proposed identity, headroom, location, capabilities and compatibility ranges; connected task creation is not itself registration acceptance.

A gateway opens its own gateway-shard database and enables the distributed data-plane client when running as gateway with a control URL; live SQL serving requires a listen address and role gateway or all.

The frontier run_start branch requires a control URL but only constructs a local aggregator, writes a startup audit event and logs fill level, without establishing a remote frontier subscription in that branch.

Library StartOptions defaults have no SQL listener whereas the executable supplies one; workers automatically wait as daemons, other background roles need daemon mode to avoid a short sleep and exit, and ROCKSTREAM_E2E_SLEEP_MS can bound both gateway and daemon lifetime.

build_runtime_object_store defaults to a local filesystem and switches to a prefix-bounded S3-compatible backend when ROCKSTREAM_OBJECT_STORE_ENDPOINT is set, requiring bucket/access/secret with an optional region; this is a separate environment contract from resolved storage.url.

Canonical lifecycle transitions are Created→Starting→Recovering→Ready→Draining→Stopping→Stopped with fatal failure paths; readiness accepts Ready or legacy Degraded, while fatal/stopped liveness codes differ from initialization or draining.

run_start creates the HTTP metrics/lifecycle probe server only when metrics_addr is present; typed control management is a separate listener enabled for listening all or daemon control with a management address.

Live run_start sets Ready after gateway startup or background setup, then on shutdown drains the tracker, aborts gateway/worker tasks, shuts down control/Raft, stops metrics and marks completion; it does not use Component::drain, and gateway startup failure marks Fatal and cleans up handles.
Successful run_start completion appends pipeline/server stop audit events and writes a support bundle before returning paths and event count.

NodeRuntime is a separate component orchestration abstraction, not the main-to-run_start live-service path; it composes by role, starts/recovers forward, reverses started components on failure, drains forward and stops in reverse, while current service wrappers largely implement state changes and failure injection.

ShutdownCoordinator supports signals and manual triggers, marks Stopped on completion, and its watchdog logs RS-3023, marks Fatal and normally exits with code 1 on deadline expiry, with explicit test suppression paths.

The root Dockerfile runs unprivileged as UID/GID 10001 in /data, defaults to all with SQL and metrics listeners, and health-checks localhost:9090/ready; exposed ports do not themselves configure live listeners.

The upgrade guide prescribes control then worker then gateway sequencing, but the rolling-upgrade qualification uses abrupt three-worker replacement and durable state/reopen validation, not graceful drain; its scope excludes control/gateway upgrades, standalone CLI transport, multiple active shards, zero query downtime and general cross-version compatibility.
Rolling-upgrade qualification rejects candidate-to-old transitions in its runner and explicitly does not establish arbitrary product on-disk downgrade detection.

Project init/new dispatch to the scaffolder for local/Kafka/PostgreSQL CDC templates; new chooses a named target directory when none is supplied, while apply and verify run separately against live endpoints.

Project apply validates version-1 manifests and referenced files, applies schema and CSV seeds over pgwire, and uses local .rockstream/applied.json content checksums to skip completed matching steps; verify executes queries and compares expected result rows.
Focused coverage includes resolver precedence/origins, configuration validation, component and binary lifecycle tests, and product-truth tests that inspect live management status membership.
